input: Find out if my employer offers tuition reimbursement

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: They may just want a yes/no confirmation, or they may need full details like reimbursement caps, eligible programs, and application steps — this changes how deep the research needs to go.
Different roles or employment types (full-time, part-time, contractor) may have different eligibility, so knowing their employment status shapes which policy applies to them.
Knowing whether they already have a specific course or degree program in mind determines whether the research needs to validate a particular expense or just survey the benefit generally.
They may not know who to contact or where to find the policy — identifying the right first step (HR portal, handbook, direct contact) is critical to getting this done quickly.
There may be a deadline pressure — such as an upcoming enrollment date — that dictates how urgently and in what order they need to act.
Their definition of 'done' could range from simply confirming the benefit exists, to having a completed application submitted — this determines how far the task needs to go.
Some people prefer to handle HR inquiries in writing (email) for a paper trail, while others prefer a quick verbal conversation — this shapes how they should reach out.

gold.taskTitle: Find out if employer offers tuition reimbursement
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to determine whether their employer has a tuition reimbursement benefit and understand how to access it.

questions.title: Do you need full benefit details or just a yes/no?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a simple confirmation that the benefit exists, or a comprehensive breakdown of limits, eligible schools, covered costs, and the application process.

questions.title: Are you full-time, part-time, or a contractor?
questions.description: Determine the user's employment status, as eligibility for tuition reimbursement often varies by employment type.

questions.title: Do you have a specific course or program in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user is researching generally or trying to get a particular course or degree covered, which affects what details matter most.

questions.title: Do you have access to an HR portal or employee handbook?
questions.description: Identify what resources the user already has available so the most direct path to the information can be recommended.

questions.title: Is there an enrollment or application deadline driving this?
questions.description: Determine whether time pressure exists that requires immediate action, such as an upcoming semester enrollment window.

questions.title: What does 'done' look like — confirmed benefit, or submitted application?
questions.description: Establish the end goal: is the task complete once the benefit is confirmed, or does the user want to go all the way through to submitting a reimbursement request?

questions.title: Do you prefer to ask HR in writing or by speaking directly?
questions.description: Understand the user's communication preference so the outreach approach — email, phone call, or in-person — matches their style and comfort level.
